# Result Description

This document describes the reported prediction errors for the fixed ensemble and its two component models at Epurun and Seosong hospitals. It is generated from the final seed-level prediction and metric CSV artifacts.

## Evaluation setup

- Ensemble: `0.55 × S11_LATENT16 + 0.45 × S04_GRU_H32_L1`
- Seeds: `42, 123, 456, 789, 1024`
- Forecast horizon and rolling step: 14 days
- Epurun: 52 folds per seed and 248 medication targets
- Seosong: 79 folds per seed and 3,126 medication targets

## Metric definitions

For ground truth $y_i$ and prediction $\hat{y}_i$ over $N$ evaluated seed–fold–horizon–medication observations:

$$\mathrm{MSE}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}(y_i-\hat{y}_i)^2$$

$$\mathrm{MAE}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}|y_i-\hat{y}_i|$$

MSE gives larger errors disproportionate influence because errors are squared. MAE is the average absolute miss in the same daily medication-demand unit as the target. Lower values are better for both metrics.

The reported ensemble MSE and MAE average the error of each of the five seeded ensemble predictions. They are not the error of the cross-seed mean prediction. Each hospital-wide value weights every seed–fold–horizon–medication observation equally. Because demand scales and target definitions differ between hospitals, raw MSE and MAE should be interpreted within each hospital rather than as a hospital ranking.

## Hospital-wide results

| Hospital | Model | Seeds | MSE | MAE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Epurun | S04 | 5 | 0.957443 | 0.406823 |
| Epurun | S11 | 5 | 0.961695 | 0.410709 |
| Epurun | Ensemble | 5 | 0.919546 | 0.404406 |
| Seosong | S04 | 5 | 2.020974 | 0.270778 |
| Seosong | S11 | 5 | 1.880985 | 0.261627 |
| Seosong | Ensemble | 5 | 1.821435 | 0.261542 |

The fixed ensemble has the lowest hospital-wide MSE at both hospitals. At Epurun it also has the lowest MAE. At Seosong the ensemble MAE is only marginally lower than S11, so the practical difference in absolute error is small. These comparisons do not change the reported negative average skill relative to the last-value naive baseline.

## Medications displayed in the prediction figures

Each hospital prediction figure displays 12 medications, one graph per row. The displayed medications are selected by the highest mean ground truth (`y_true`) over the rolling evaluation period. This is a demand-volume display rule, not a ranking of model quality. The medication-level MSE and MAE use all five seeded ensemble predictions, consistent with the hospital-wide results.

## Interpretation limits

Medication-level MSE and MAE reveal heterogeneity hidden by the hospital-wide average, but they do not encode medication importance, shortage cost, or clinical severity. Targets with larger numerical demand can dominate squared-error summaries. The values are retrospective rolling-evaluation results and should not be interpreted as calibrated clinical risk estimates.
